Case file — Retail Analytics

Where is the Superstore actually losing money?

Solo project · Jun–Jul 2025

Superstore Sales Analytics & Customer Segmentation

9,994 orders · 793 customers · US market, 2011–2014

Four years of retail transactions, cleaned and pushed through EDA, RFM customer segmentation, and an interactive Power BI dashboard — turning raw sales rows into a profitability and customer-targeting story.

PythonpandasPower BIDAXRFM
  1. Cleaned data types, removed redundant columns, checked Sales/Quantity/Profit for invalid values.
  2. Engineered Profit Margin and Discount Range features; broke down profitability by category, region, and segment.
  3. Ran monthly and quarterly time-series analysis (2011–2014) to surface seasonality and YoY growth.
  4. Built an RFM scoring pipeline in Python, sorting customers into 9 behavioral segments.
  5. Shipped an interactive Power BI dashboard with custom DAX measures and dynamic filters.
>30% discount — the threshold where most sub-categories tip into net loss.
Tables & Bookcases — the two consistent loss-making sub-categories.
12% of customers ("Champions") drive over 40% of total revenue.

Case file — Demand Analysis

Which factors actually drive bike-sharing demand?

Solo project · Jan–Feb 2025

Yulu Bike Sharing — Demand Analysis & Hypothesis Testing

10,886 hourly records · weather, season, holiday & workingday variables

A statistical demand study for a bike-sharing service — using ANOVA and Tukey HSD to quantify which operational and environmental factors move ridership, then translating that into fleet and pricing calls.

PythonSciPyANOVATukey HSDseaborn
  1. Cleaned and validated 10,886 hourly records; engineered datetime-derived features and removed invalid weather entries.
  2. Used boxplots to explore ridership across weekday, hour-of-day, season, holiday, and workingday.
  3. Ran one-way ANOVA and Tukey HSD post-hoc tests to confirm differences across time-of-day, season, and weather groups.
  4. Checked correlations between ridership and weather variables via Pearson correlation and regression plots.
  5. Translated the statistics into fleet allocation and time-based pricing recommendations.
Two daily peaks — 8 AM and 4–6 PM, matching commute patterns.
p < 0.05 — season and weather significantly affect ridership (ANOVA).
Workingdays ≠ weekends — hourly demand shape differs significantly (Tukey HSD).
No Power BI dashboard for this project — analysis lives entirely in the notebook. Full EDA, test statistics, and charts are on GitHub.

Case file — Diagnostic Classification

Which tumor traits separate malignant from benign?

Solo project · Sep–Dec 2024

Breast Cancer Diagnosis — Statistical Analysis & Classification

569 patient records · 30 tumor morphology features · Wisconsin Diagnostic dataset

Combines hypothesis testing with classic ML on tumor morphology data to find which features best distinguish malignant from benign cases, then makes the pattern visible to a non-technical audience via Power BI.

Pythonscikit-learnANOVATukey HSDPower BI
Educational / portfolio use only — not for clinical diagnosis
  1. Ran frequency-distribution and skewness analysis on 30 features across 569 records; removed outliers with the IQR method.
  2. Applied ANOVA to test whether radius_mean and smoothness_mean differ between malignant and benign cases, then Tukey HSD for pairwise comparison by tumor-size category.
  3. Built and evaluated Decision Tree and Logistic Regression classifiers to predict diagnosis from tumor features.
  4. Visualized diagnostic feature patterns in a Power BI dashboard for non-technical stakeholders.
85% accuracy — Logistic Regression on the held-out test set.
p < 0.05 — radius_mean and smoothness_mean both differ significantly by diagnosis.
Larger tumor size — strongly associated with malignant diagnosis (Tukey HSD).
